title: Seems like no matter how much I ask GPT to make a distinct image... it comes out signature grainy pixel after an edit.
author: Chacudno
selftext:
Lets say I ask for a high detail 2d illustration of an RPG character. It makes a decent concept. If I ask it to change something minor, the next image has that grain.

Any tips for avoiding that? It does the same for environments, i really want to achieve more of a fire emblem three houses type look.

comments.author: kilographix
comments.body: You could try generating it in parts and fusing thwm together manually with something like paint.NET

replies.author: Chacudno
replies.body: Yeah I've had to blend before, was just looking for something more fluid.

comments.author: Mindestiny
comments.body:
The problem is the way ChatGPT processes edits.  

It *used to* re-generate the entire image and just attempt to change the one thing that you asked it to change.  This of course led to the new output leaking subtle edits into the entire image as a natural artifact of re-generating the entire thing.

Now they've tried to implement some kind of smart masking to do inpainting where it *just* detects and masks off the portion you asked to edit and re-generates just that part before fusing it back together.  This of course has the new output often denoising at too high a strength and you get a clear contrast between the new and old segments of the image.

Basically this is just the wrong tool for that kind of job.  It's swinging a sledgehammer at a finishing nail.

replies.author: Chacudno
replies.body: The process you explained makes sense thats how its working. Terrible method though. Alternative suggestions?

replies.author: Mindestiny
replies.body: Local generation tools where you can control the inpainting specifically.

comments.author: KillaNugs
comments.body: You need to establish an art bible for your project  first.

comments.author: EmotionalFan5429
comments.body: Simple solution: don't use ChatGPT. There are a lot of alternatives like Flux 2, Qwen image edit, Krea, Ideogram. Even Nano Banana is better!

comments.author: Big_River_
comments.body: you are not do right - I work with chatgpt and never have this issue at all - always recommend you minimax

comments.author: Nasilbitatbirakti
comments.body: No way to avoid it I think. That's why I'm using gemini to generate images.

replies.author: Chacudno
replies.body: Just redid my images with Gemini, its much better visually. Does not do well with precise edits but its better than GPT in a lot of ways, I think i can combine the 2 to get things done.

replies.author: Nasilbitatbirakti
replies.body: The only weakness of Gemini is it can't do true transparent background. You can remove it with other tools but if you have really detailed edges then you're gonna have visual errors. Chatgpt is great at removing very small spots and doing (semi)transparent material like glasses and liquids and such. After I get the final image in Gemini I just run it through gpt to make it perfectly transparent.

comments.author: RoryOS
comments.body: The only thing I like about chat gpt image Gen it's that or can do transparent pixels

comments.author: BansheeTheGame
comments.body: GPT can still be useful for quick references or concept exploration, but I’d move the image into a dedicated image model for iterative edits and cleanup. ChatGPT is a general-purpose tool; it’s unlikely to be the best option for every stage of an art workflow.
